out.headline: Investment Diligence Memo: Atomberg Technologies Limited
out.summary: Atomberg Technologies Limited operates in the consumer electrical appliances sector, focusing on fans and BLDC motors with promoters Manoj Kumar Meena and Sibabrata Das [p. 309]. For Fiscal 2026, the company reported a restated loss before tax and loss after tax of 1,488.81 million INR [p. 83, p. 400], following a restated loss after tax of 1,174.05 million INR for the year ended March 31, 2025 [p. 83]. Total equity stood at 1,861.46 million INR in Fiscal 2026, alongside current borrowings of 2,397.53 million INR and non-current borrowings of 177.75 million INR [p. 34, p. 375]. The proposed fresh issue aims to raise up to 4,500.00 million INR to repay certain borrowings, fund brand awareness, invest in research and development, and for general corporate purposes, alongside an offer for sale of up to 76,541,851 equity shares [p. 150].
red_flags: Restated loss after tax was 1,488.81 million INR for Fiscal 2026 [p. 83].
Aggregate amount involved in outstanding material civil litigations against the company is 3,776.84 million INR [p. 50].
Current borrowings of 2,397.53 million INR and non-current borrowings of 177.75 million INR exceed the total equity of 1,861.46 million INR [p. 34, p. 375].
Finance costs were 449.07 million INR in Fiscal 2026 against a loss before tax of 1,488.81 million INR [p. 400].
Trade receivables increased to 2,389.05 million INR in Fiscal 2026 from 1,755.71 million INR as at March 31, 2025 [p. 345, p. 358].
There is 1 material civil litigation pending against the Promoters [p. 50].
questions_for_management: How does management plan to achieve operational profitability given the restated loss of 1,488.81 million INR in Fiscal 2026 [p. 83]?
What is the specific breakdown of the 3,776.84 million INR in outstanding material civil litigations against the company and what are the expected timelines for resolution [p. 50]?

With current borrowings at 2,397.53 million INR and finance costs at 449.07 million INR, how much of the up to 4,500.00 million INR fresh issue proceeds will be allocated specifically to debt repayment [p. 34, p. 150, p. 400]?
What are the underlying reasons for the increase in trade receivables from 1,755.71 million INR in Fiscal 2025 to 2,389.05 million INR in Fiscal 2026 [p. 345, p. 358]?
Can management provide details regarding the 1 material civil litigation pending against the promoters and its potential impact on the company [p. 50]?
